MAJOR: finalize_item writes `item_revision = revision + 1` and gate2 `completion_gaps` compares it to the live revision. Any backlog write between finalize and merge (status, delivery, note) bumps revision → permanent `FINAL_REPORT_STALE` hard-block on merge; the contract is an off-by-one race, not a durable snapshot.

gate_decisions derives mode with `int(gate)`: gate "1.5"/"2.5" either raises ValueError inside decision recording or silently maps to the wrong mode, so disposition policy runs against the wrong finding set.

Gate 2 enforces only diff-mode policy (design-mode violations recorded post-Gate-1 pass Gate 2 and are caught only by finalize/trail-check) — the three enforcement points are not equivalent, contrary to the AC.
`completion_gaps` is an early `continue` before design-evidence/churn checks in gate2_completion_check.check, so only the first failing dimension is reported and other merge blockers are masked.
MINOR: AC-completeness logic is duplicated in gate_decisions.py (gate 2) and finalize_item.py `ac_problems` — two sources of truth that will drift.
execution_trail_check imports `core.backlog` inside the per-item loop and rebuilds the backlog lambda per item/mode; hoist to module scope (also avoids repeated imports in a loop).
finalize_item mixes a count message (`"only N of M ACs recorded"`) into `ac_problems`, then prints every entry as "AC not PASS" — misleading diagnostics.
final_report embeds the same test dicts twice (`tests` and `tests_by_kind.rows`), bloating the persisted item record and the store.
test_deferred_needs_id_and_approval uses the item's own id (BI-PF-1484) as the "external" follow-up because the fixture lacks an `id` key — the self-reference exclusion path is never exercised.
NIT: review-dispositions.json `approval_decision`/`approval_scope` duplicate literals already hardcoded in disposition_decide.py; the config is not fully authoritative.
SUMMARY: Well-scoped, AC-aligned change; language rule respected (tooling Python + permitted edit to shipped Python); cap/approval policy, final-report persistence and completion guards are tested.

Top risks: revision-coupled `FINAL_REPORT_STALE` check can hard-block merges after any legitimate backlog write; fragile gate→mode derivation for 1.5/2.5; duplicated AC-completeness logic across gate_decisions and finalize_item.
Recommend fixing the revision/snapshot contract and centralizing AC + policy checks into one shared module before merge.
